{{Short description|Treatise by Piero della Francesca}}
{{Expand French|De prospectiva pingendi|topic=sci|date=April 2019}}
{{italictitle}}
[[File:Piero, proiezioni di una testa scorciata dal de prospectiva pingendi, ante 1482, milano, biblioteca ambrosiana.jpg|thumb|250px| Perspective of anatomy from ''De prospectiva Pingendi''.]]
[[File:De la perspective en peinture.jpg|thumb|250px|An [[icosahedron]] in perspective from ''De prospectiva pingendi'']]

'''''De prospectiva pingendi''''' (''On the Perspective of Painting'') is the earliest and only pre-1500 Renaissance treatise solely devoted to the subject of perspective.<ref>{{cite book|last=Andersen|first=Kirsti|title=The Geometry of Art|url=https://archive.org/details/geometryarthisto00ande|url-access=limited|year=2007|publisher=Springer|location=New York, NY|isbn=978-0-387-25961-1|page=[https://archive.org/details/geometryarthisto00ande/page/n49 17]}}</ref> It was written by the Italian master [[Piero della Francesca]] in the mid-1470s to 1480s,<ref name=livio>{{cite book|last=Livio|first=Mario|author-link=Mario Livio|title=The Golden Ratio|publisher=[[Random House|Broadway Books]]|location=New York|year=2003|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=bUARfgWRH14C&pg=PA126|isbn=0-7679-0816-3|page=126}}</ref> and possibly by about 1474.<ref>{{cite book|last=Kemp|first=Martin|author-link=Martin Kemp (art historian)|title=The Science of Art|url=https://archive.org/details/scienceofartopti0000kemp|url-access=registration|date=1990|publisher=Yale University Press|location=New Haven and London|isbn=0-300-05241-3|page=[https://archive.org/details/scienceofartopti0000kemp/page/27 27]}}</ref> Despite its Latin title, the text is written in Italian.

==The book==
The subjects covered by Piero della Francesca in these writings include [[arithmetic]], [[algebra]], [[geometry]] and innovative work in both [[solid geometry]] and [[Perspective (graphical)|perspective]].<ref name="D">[http://www.codicesillustres.com/catalogue/de_prospectiva_pingendi/], Codices Illustres</ref><ref name=E/>

The script consists of three parts:
* Part One ''Disegno'', describing techniques for painting faces
* Part Two ''Commensurazio'', describing perspectives
* Part Three ''Coloro'', describing techniques for creating perspectives by using colours

==History==
{{further|Mathematics and art}}

''De prospectiva pingendi'' was probably created in the years between 1474 until 1482.<ref name=B>{{cite web|url=http://www.dartmouth.edu/~matc/math5.geometry/unit13/unit13.html#Francesca|title=Geometry in Art & Architecture Unit 13|last=Calter|first=Paul|year=1998|website=Dartmouth College|access-date=December 23, 2018|archive-date=April 3, 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100403055857/http://www.dartmouth.edu/~matc/math5.geometry/unit13/unit13.html#Francesca|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="A">[http://www.britannica.com/EBchecked/topic/428630/On-Perspective-in-Painting], Encyclopædia Britannica</ref><ref name=E/>

The writings were inspired by the book ''[[De pictura]]'' by [[Leon Battista Alberti]]<ref name=A/> and references [[Euclid]]'s ''[[Euclid's Elements|Elements]]'' and ''[[Euclid's Optics|Optics]]''.<ref name=livio/><ref name=E>{{cite web |url=http://emsh.calarts.edu/alumni/bkeresey/pier.html |title=Archived copy |access-date=2010-04-11 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100329120658/http://emsh.calarts.edu/alumni/bkeresey/pier.html |archive-date=2010-03-29 }}, Computer Animation Lab</ref> The manuscript later came into the possession of the [[Biblioteca Palatina]] in [[Parma]]<ref name=E/> before it was transferred to the [[Biblioteca Ambrosiana]].

Much of Piero's work was later absorbed into the writing of others, notably [[Luca Pacioli]], whose ''[[Divina proportione]]'' (1509) discusses Piero's use of perspective, as well featuring an uncredited translation of Piero's entire work on solid geometry, ''[[De quinque corporibus regularibus]]''.

In 1899 the work was first published in book form.<ref name="C">[https://books.google.com/books?id=Bnh3FKIKT9AC&pg=PA606], Google Books.com</ref>
